question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> be the set of all solutions of the equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mfenced><msqrt><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></munder><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Given equation is:

cos-12x-2cos-11-x2=π,x∈-12,12

It is possible if

cos-12x=π    ....(1)

and  2cos-11-x2=0    ....(2)

From equation (1), x=-12 which is not satisfying equation (2).

So, no such x exists.
